newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe steelmakers plan to boost can recycling.
newsitem.headline: Europe steelmakers plan to boost can recycling.

text.p: APEAL, the group of European manufacturers of packaging steel, expects its can recycling rates to rise to 60 percent in the year 2005 from an estimated 45 percent in 1995, a statement issued in Germany said.

A spokesman for the tinplate information centre, APEAL's German partner, said planned improvements of waste reclamation systems and a stable steel pricing structure made the industry confident its forecast would materialise.
Recycling of aluminium, steel's fiercest competitor in drinks can applications, hinged on the volatile aluminium price which decided aluminium scrap trade flows, he said.
The European tinplate can recycling rate in 1995 was 41 percent in 1995, up from 34 percent in 1994, APEAL data showed.
This already exceeded legal stipulations, which demand a recycling rate of just 15 percent by 2001 in the EU, it said.
Germany's leading rate of 67 percent in 1995 compared with 58 percent in the Netherlands, 40 percent in France and 16 percent in Britain.
Drinks cans made of tinplated steel would account for 21 billion of the total 37 billion produced in Europe this year.
The steel can has overtaken its rival aluminium in Europe with a 55 percent share this year, up from 45 percent a year ago as producers convinced customers to convert can production lines to steel.
